common_name: Conger Yellow Tea Olive (Large-Leaved Butter-Yellow Fragrant Osmanthus)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring or fall in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; this vigorous, upright selection benefits from an annual light shearing after its heaviest bloom flush to keep a dense, columnar habit.

directions: Site Conger Yellow along a walkway or near a patio where its heavy clusters of butter-yellow, apricot-scented flowers can be appreciated up close, since the individual blooms are tiny despite their outsized fragrance. This selection carries noticeably larger, darker leaves than typical seed-grown tea olive and blooms most heavily in spring and fall with scattered flushes through the rest of the year in mild Gulf Coast winters. It forms a dense, upright oval to columnar shrub over time and tolerates shearing well if a hedge or more formal shape is wanted. Give it consistent moisture during establishment, but once rooted in it handles routine dry spells with little fuss.
sources: Clemson Cooperative Extension Home & Garden Information Center

common_name: Big-Flowered Banana Shrub (Long-Lasting Purple-Flowered Banana Magnolia)

planting.note: Plant container-grown specimens in spring in moist, slightly acidic, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; this variety is somewhat less cold-tolerant than the typical creamy-flowered form, so give it a sheltered spot at the northern edge of its range.

directions: This botanical variety of banana shrub is distinguished from the typical creamy-yellow form by flowers that open a much darker rose-to-wine purple and, notably, persist open for two to three days rather than the single day typical of the species, giving a longer, more visible bloom display alongside the trademark banana-custard fragrance. Its leaves tend to be thicker and glossier and the overall habit denser, making it a good specimen or informal screen where both color and scent are wanted at close range. Plant it where afternoon shade tempers the harshest summer sun, since foliage can bleach yellow-green under constant full exposure, and avoid heavy pruning since flowers form on older wood.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (International Dendrology Society)

common_name: Stubbs Purple Banana Shrub (Compact Purple-Flowered Banana Magnolia)

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container stock in spring in fertile, humus-rich, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in partial shade to full sun; this selection was chosen in part for a hardier, more compact habit than typical crassipes forms.

directions: Stubbs Purple is a compact selection of the purple-flowered banana shrub variety, prized by collectors for tepals that open a deeper, more saturated purple than the species while keeping the same dense, tidy, slow-growing frame that makes banana shrub such a low-fuss foundation plant. Its smaller mature size compared to straight var. crassipes fits it well into mixed borders or smaller courtyard gardens where the intense banana-like fragrance can still be enjoyed at close range each spring. Grow it in humus-rich, evenly moist but well-drained soil, and resist the urge to prune hard, since flower buds set on the previous season's growth.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (International Dendrology Society)

common_name: Purple Queen Banana Shrub (Dark Red-Purple Banana Magnolia)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in fertile, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; foliage runs noticeably darker green than typical banana shrub, which helps the deep purple flowers stand out.

directions: Selected as an open-pollinated seedling for exceptionally dark, red-purple flowers that fade gradually to cream as they age, Purple Queen offers the showiest bloom color of the banana shrub cultivars while retaining the classic, intensely sweet banana-custard fragrance. Its darker foliage also makes an attractive year-round backdrop even between bloom flushes in spring and early summer. It performs best with regular moisture and a spot that gets some protection from the most intense midday sun in the Gulf Coast climate, though it tolerates full sun where soil moisture is reliable. Established plants need little more than an occasional light shaping after flowering.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (International Dendrology Society)

common_name: Maudiae Michelia (Smiling Monkey Tree, Fragrant White-Flowered Evergreen Magnolia)

planting.note: Plant container-grown specimens in spring in fertile, humus-rich, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade, choosing a site with room for it to develop into a small tree over time.

directions: Michelia maudiae is a fast-growing, well-shaped evergreen relative of magnolia grown for its early-spring display of large, open, heavily fragrant white flowers set against distinctive blue-green foliage. Unlike many magnolia relatives it flowers reliably while still young, so gardeners are not left waiting years for the first bloom. It develops a somewhat narrow, upright habit that suits use as a specimen tree, screen, or street tree where space allows it to reach its mature height. It adapts to a fairly wide range of soil conditions once established but benefits from a wind-sheltered site at the cooler edge of its hardiness range, and requires little pruning beyond removing any damaged wood.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (International Dendrology Society)

common_name: Sweet Michelia (Doltsopa Magnolia, Large Fragrant White-Flowered Evergreen Tree)

planting.note: Plant container-grown trees in spring in fertile, humus-rich, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun, allowing ample room for its eventual size and multi-stemmed spreading form.

directions: Sweet Michelia is a large, fast-growing, multi-stemmed evergreen tree that produces an unusually long winter-to-spring bloom season of large, showy, intensely fragrant creamy-white flowers borne directly along the branches. Its glossy, leathery, dark green leaves with rusty-brown, fuzzy undersides give it strong year-round structure even between bloom cycles. Because of its eventual size it is best used as a specimen or shade tree rather than a foundation planting, and it responds well to regular watering during its establishment years. Once established it needs comparatively little maintenance beyond occasional structural pruning to maintain a strong branch framework.
sources: Urban Tree Farm Nursery Plant Database

common_name: Coco Michelia (Compact Hybrid Banana-Scented Evergreen Shrub)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in fertile, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in full sun to partial shade; mulch and fertilize lightly at planting to help establish this tight, tidy grower.

directions: Sometimes called coconut magnolia for its sweet, tropical fragrance, 'Coco' is a compact hybrid selection related to true banana shrub with cream flowers and glossy foliage that both run slightly larger than the species. Its tight, dense growth habit and manageable mature size make it a good fit for containers or for clipping into a low hedge or screen where space is at a premium. It blooms over an extended spring-into-summer period, releasing its scent most strongly on warm, still, humid days. It tolerates a range of light conditions from full sun to partial shade and asks for little beyond routine watering and an occasional light shaping.
